name: Spatially Varying Gaussian Splatting (SVGS)
definition: A method that utilizes spatially varying colors and opacity within a single Gaussian primitive to improve representation ability, addressing the non-compactness of vanilla Gaussian Splatting where primitives have only a single view-dependent color and opacity.
summary: Spatially Varying Gaussian Splatting enhances representation by defining color and opacity as spatially varying functions of the intersection point, allowing a single primitive to fit complex textures.
